headline: Trial run. A theory-heavy day: Kleinberg & Wei on breadth in language generation, Blondel et al. on why sequence-level losses for autoregressive LMs break, a representation-theory account of what diagonal SSMs cannot track, and a vector-search stopping rule with an exactness guarantee.

daily_picks.title: Gradient Equilibrium in Online Learning: Theory and Applications
daily_picks.digest:
Setting and problem 
 The protocol is the standard adversarial online learning one, stripped of its usual objective. At each round $t=1,2,3,\dots$ the environment fixes a loss $\ell_t:\mathbb{R}^d\to(-\infty,\infty]$, assumed finite and subdifferentiable on a common domain $D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d$; typically $\ell_t$ is induced by a data point $(x_t,y_t)$, e.g. $\ell_t(\theta)=\tfrac12(y_t-x_t^\mathsf{T}\theta)^2$, but that dependence is suppressed. The learner plays $\theta_t\in D$ using only information through round $t-1$, then $\ell_t$ is revealed and a vector $g_t(\theta_t)$ is computed. Crucially, $g_t(\theta)$ is a generalized (Rockafellar–Wets "regular") subgradient: any $v$ with $\liminf_{z\to\theta}\big(\ell(z)-\ell(\theta)-v^\mathsf{T}(z-\theta)\big)/|z-\theta|_2\ge 0$. This covers convex subgradients and gradients of differentiable, possibly nonconvex losses. No convexity is assumed anywhere in the main theory, and no stochastic or generative model for the sequence : the guarantees are per-sequence, pathwise, and hold under arbitrary drift or adversarial play.

daily_picks.title: Approximate Top-$k$ for Increased Parallelism
daily_picks.digest:
Setting and problem 
 The object of study is the top-$k$ primitive itself, viewed as a parallel kernel rather than as an algorithmic complexity question. Input: a batch of $m$ vectors of length $n$ (shape $(m,n)$, in float32 or bfloat16 on a GPU); output: $k$ (value, index) pairs. Exact top-$k$ requires the returned set to be $\mathrm{argtop} k(x)$; this paper relaxes that and measures quality by recall $R(k,b,k_b)=Z(k,b,k_b)/k$, where $Z$ counts how many of the true top-$k$ values the approximate method returns. Cost is measured three ways: achieved memory bandwidth (minimum bytes that must move, divided by runtime), wall-clock duration, and a family of hand-built abstract operation-counting cost models $C $.}}, C_{\mathrm{serial}}, C_{\mathrm{parallel}


 The algorithm class is bucketed top-$k$ , two stages:


 
 Stage 1 : partition ${0,\dots,n-1}$ into $b$ buckets via an assignment map $B$, take the largest $k_b$ values in each bucket independently, concatenate the $b\cdot k_b$ survivors. 
 Stage 2 : if $b\cdot k_b > k$, run an exact top-$k$ on those $b\cdot k_b$ candidates. 
 
 Design parameters: $b\in{1,\dots,n}$, $k_b\in{1,\dots,\min(k,n/b)}$, subject to $b\cdot k_b\ge k$; the over-collection ratio $b\cdot k_b/k$ is the knob that trades cost for recall. Two further axes: the assignment map — contiguous , $B(i)=\lfloor ib/n\rfloor$, versus interleaved , $B(i)=i \bmod b$ — …

daily_picks.title: Tracing Attention Computation Through Feature Interactions
daily_picks.digest:
Setting and problem 
 The object of study is a single attention head's pre-softmax score. For residual-stream vectors $x_{p_q}, x_{p_k} \in \mathbb{R}^{d}$ at a query position $p_q$ and key position $p_k$, the head computes


 $$\mathrm{score}(p_k, p_q) \;=\; x_{p_q}^{\top} W_{QK}\, x_{p_k}, \qquad W_{QK} = W_Q^{\top} W_K ,$$


 i.e. a bilinear form on the residual stream, with $W_{QK}$ the low-rank combined matrix from Elhage et al.'s A Mathematical Framework . The analyst is given a trained model — here Claude 3.5 Haiku — its activations on a prompt, and a dictionary of sparsely active features with decoder vectors, so that at each position $x_p = \sum_f a_f(p) v_f + b + e_p$, where $a_f(p)$ are (mostly zero) feature activations, $v_f$ dictionary/decoder vectors, $b$ a bias, and $e_p$ the dictionary's reconstruction error. The method must output a human-readable account of why this head attended here and not elsewhere , and must plug that account into an existing attribution graph.


 The motivating gap is specific. Anthropic's attribution-graph line (circuit tracing / Biology of a Large Language Model ) built interpretable causal graphs on top of cross-layer transcoders that replace MLPs. researchers.title: Sketching Language Models for Context Attribution
researchers.summary: Tight bounds for sketching leave-one-out context attribution.

researchers.title: Measuring, Revealing and Mitigating Harmful Content Propagation in Recommender Systems
researchers.comments: This work has been acceptted by IEEE TPAMI
researchers.summary: Measuring and mitigating harmful-content propagation in recommender systems (TPAMI).

researchers.title: KuaiRecV2: Benchmarking Large-Scale Continual Learning for Diversified and Multi-task Recommendation
researchers.comments: This paper has been accepted to NeurIPS 2026
researchers.curator_blurb: Kuaishou releases a video benchmark for testing recommenders on continual learning, diversity, and multiple tasks.
researchers.evidence: Kuaishou paper; co-authors Fan Yang, Han Li
researchers.summary: KuaiRecV2 benchmark for continual multi-task recommendation.

papers.title: Characterizing Local Breadth in Language Generation
papers.summary: In the Kleinberg–Mullainathan generation-in-the-limit model, measures breadth by lower Banach density and characterises the optimal achievable breadth exactly in 1-D; in d≥2 there is no single best generator, and the full region of achievable density profiles is characterised.
papers.why: Clean validity–breadth (hallucination vs. mode collapse) theory from Kleinberg; the 'no single best generator in d≥2' result is the surprise.

papers.title: On the Difficulty of Sequence-Level Supervised Learning for Autoregressive Language Models
papers.summary: Shows the two natural sequence-level losses that bake greedy decoding or sampling into training are unbounded below, links them via autoregressive Gumbel tricks, and proves the stop-gradient 'moment matching' direction is a valid descent direction for NLL in function space — but too noisy, so teacher forcing stays.
papers.why: A crisp negative result on exposure bias with a real proof; relevant to any sequence-level objective, including generative retrieval decoding.

papers.title: Symmetry in Time: A Representation Theory of Linear Recurrent Memory
papers.summary: Treats an SSM's state update as a linear representation of the input monoid: an SSM tracks a group exactly when the group is a quotient of the group its transition matrices generate, so diagonal real/complex SSMs track only commutative groups; quaternion blocks (HyperSSM) fix S5 tracking.
papers.why: A neat algebraic characterisation of state-tracking limits, in the line of 'what can transformers/SSMs represent'.

papers.title: Sketching Language Models for Context Attribution
papers.summary: Estimates all leave-one-out context-attribution values of an n-token prompt with O(√log(1/ε)/ε) model calls under a stability assumption, with a matching lower bound, via sketching arithmetic circuits with decaying Taylor coefficients.
papers.why: Tight upper/lower bounds for an LM-querying problem, evaluated on a retrieval task; co-authored by Grigoris Velegkas (followed).

papers.title: Calibrated Early Termination with Bounded Optimality Gaps for Constrained Vector Search
papers.comments: 14 pages, 5 figures, 3 tables. Code available at https://github.com/zhangshea/CaST
papers.summary: Early termination for (constrained) k-NN on graph indexes with a guarantee that the answer is exact with probability ≥1−ε; risk-constrained stopping becomes an LP over an order polytope whose Lagrangian minimisers are staircase rules computed by DP, then calibrated with fixed-sequence binomial tests, plus a lower bound on the optimum of the rule family.
papers.why: Rare vector-search paper with a provable exactness target instead of average recall, and an optimality lower bound.

papers.title: Two mathematical models of knowledge distillation
papers.summary: Two analysable models of knowledge distillation (GLMs under SGD; rank-1 matrix approximation) showing distillation helps by making optimisation faster, not by generalising better.
papers.why: Duchi & Schmidt on a question behind much LLM post-training: what distillation actually buys.

papers.title: When and How SignSGD Outperforms SGD: A Functional Scaling Law Perspective
papers.comments: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026 as a spotlight paper
papers.summary: Functional scaling law for SignSGD in power-law kernel regression: gradient noise smooths the sign, acting as a preconditioner that maps H to H^{1/2}; faster signal learning, slower noise forgetting, giving regime-dependent advantages over SGD.
papers.why: Scaling-law theory that explains batch-size behaviour of sign-based (Adam-like) optimisers.

papers.title: Tokenization: Hardness and Bicriteria Approximation Algorithms
papers.summary: Binary tokenization (choose ≤K substrings minimising token count) has no polynomial n^{1−ε}-approximation unless P=NP; gives (γ,γ)-bicriteria algorithms with γ=√M log n, and a storage-budget variant.
papers.why: Tokenization theory — inapproximability plus matching-style bicriteria algorithms.

papers.title: Finding the Farthest in High Dimensions: Dynamic Diameter and Farthest-Neighbor Search
papers.summary: Dynamic c-approximate diameter and farthest-neighbour search in high dimensions with better update/space exponents than Indyk (SODA'03), robust to adaptive updates.
papers.why: Algorithmic, but the high-dimensional NN machinery is close to MIPS/ANN theory.

papers.title: From Link Prediction to Linear Community Detection: A Finite-Sample Guarantee for Graph Pretraining
papers.comments: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026. 47 pages, 8 figures. Code: https://github.com/YChen1103/LP-to-Linear-Community-Detection
papers.summary: In a finite-sample SBM, small held-out link-prediction risk with a bilinear decoder implies small error for linear community classification on the learned embeddings, with explicit Õ(√(d/n)) terms.
papers.why: A theory of why an edge-level dot-product objective yields linearly useful embeddings — close to retrieval/recsys embedding questions.

papers.title: Sharp Covering-Number Bounds for Feedforward ReLU Networks via Parameter Symmetries
papers.summary: Characterises all parameter symmetries of (leaky) ReLU nets (positive channel scaling and permutation) and turns them into sharp covering-number bounds: exponent S−H and a G! divisor, with matching lower bounds.

papers.title: Towards a Theory of Learnability via Debate
papers.summary: Formulates learning from a debate-judging human as online learning; shows adversarial debate is not always the best way to learn, and characterises a cooperative protocol's learnability by a combinatorial dimension.

papers.title: A Matching Lower Bound for Online Smooth Calibration
papers.summary: Closes the gap for online smooth calibration: a new adversary forces Ω(√T) error, matching the known upper bound.

papers.title: Same-State Pairs Make One JEPA Proof of the Platonic Representation Hypothesis Vacuous
papers.summary: Shows that with same-state positive pairs the JEPA proof of the Platonic Representation Hypothesis becomes vacuous (every whitened state function is a minimiser); one of four quantitative results survives.

papers.title: Trait Hitchhiking in LLM Post-Training
papers.summary: Models how RL post-training amplifies or suppresses untargeted 'traits' using the Price equation from evolutionary biology; the Price estimate tracks trait dynamics under GRPO.

papers.title: Pretraining Data Statistics Shape the Phases of Learning Entity Comparison in Language Models
papers.summary: Small LMs learn entity comparison in three data-determined phases — pick by frequency, then by position, then correctly; Zipfian vs uniform entity frequency changes the phases.

papers.title: Evaluating Compositional Generalization in Transformers: The Role of Composition Equivalence and Module Coverage
papers.comments: 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026). Track on Evaluations and Datasets
papers.summary: Apparent compositional generalization of transformers mostly exploits 'composition equivalences' (different module sequences, same function); removing them collapses performance.

papers.title: When Direction Matters: Diagnosing Relational Instruction Following in Dense Retrieval
papers.curator_blurb: Shows that dense retrievers follow keyword-based instructions but often fail when an instruction only reverses a relation over the same entities.
papers.summary: SwitchIR: dense and late-interaction retrievers follow lexical/attribute instructions but fail when only the direction of a relation flips; an exact margin decomposition locates the failure.

papers.title: Search-by-Answer Bias in Retrieval Models
papers.curator_blurb: Shows that dense retrievers can favor passages containing answers their backbone model already knows, even over passages stating the queried relation.
papers.summary: Dense retrievers favour passages containing answers their backbone LM already knows, even over passages that state the answer — a 'search-by-answer' bias.

papers.title: ReSID: Rethinking Long-Tail Retrieval in Generative Recommendation through Item Reachability
papers.curator_blurb: Alibaba helps generative recommenders reach long-tail items with parallel semantic IDs, debiased search, and partial matching.
papers.summary: Long-tail reachability in generative recommendation: parallel SIDs beat sequential ones on tail items; beam search pruning bounds recovery.

papers.title: RoutingTrie: Metadata Routing for Constrained Generative Retrieval
papers.curator_blurb: Shopify applies metadata constraints before beam selection in generative retrieval, using compact per-field indexes on a shared semantic ID trie.
papers.summary: Shopify: metadata constraints applied before beam selection in generative retrieval.

papers.title: Not All Branches Are Equal: Adaptive Semantic ID Construction for Generative Recommendation
papers.curator_blurb: Builds semantic IDs as tree paths, choosing each node's number of branches by maximizing the silhouette coefficient instead of using a fixed branching factor.
papers.summary: Semantic IDs as tree paths with an adaptive branching factor per node.

papers.title: TS-GEAR: Taobao Shangou GEnerative Ad Retrieval
papers.curator_blurb: Alibaba proposes a generative retrieval framework for delivery search ads.
papers.summary: Alibaba generative ad retrieval for delivery search.

papers.title: RecoGEM: A Serving System for Production-Scale Generative Recommendation
papers.curator_blurb: Presents a production serving system for generative recommendation in which a runtime manages candidate state and live updates, and a separate engine speeds up attention and selection.
papers.summary: Production serving system for generative recommendation.

papers.title: From Tokens to Behaviors: Rethinking Generative Recommendation for User Trajectory Prediction
papers.curator_blurb: Proposes a generative recommender that predicts a user's future behavior sequence, not just the next item.
papers.summary: Predicts a user's future behaviour sequence rather than only the next item.

papers.title: TriGen: A Generative Paradigm for Trigger-Induced Recommendation
papers.curator_blurb: Alibaba introduces a generative recommender for the e-commerce follow-up feed opened by a click.
papers.summary: Alibaba generative recommender for trigger-induced (click-opened) feeds.

papers.title: SepLRM: A Foundation Model Paradigm for Recommendation
papers.curator_blurb: ByteDance splits large recommendation models into one shared model that encodes long user histories once and exports a KV cache, plus vertical models that query it.
papers.summary: ByteDance splits large rec models into a shared long-history encoder and light task models.

papers.title: REWEAVE: Online Learning for Workload-Adaptive HNSW Indexes
papers.comments: 20 pages, 9 figures, 5 tables. Full version with appendix
papers.curator_blurb: Introduces an online method that learns which HNSW edges matter for the query workload and rewires them within the same per-node degree cap, improving recall on skewed or shifting queries.
papers.summary: Online rewiring of HNSW edges for skewed or shifting query workloads under the same degree cap.

papers.title: HyperPage: Learned Page Layouts for Disk-Resident Graph Vector Indexes
papers.comments: 14 pages, 4 figures, 7 tables. Code available at: https://github.com/zhangshea/HyperPage
papers.summary: Learned page layouts for disk-resident graph indexes (DiskANN-style) from traversal logs.

papers.title: Authenticated Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search in Outsourced Vector Databases
papers.summary: Authenticated graph-based ANN for outsourced vector DBs using vector commitments.

papers.title: VecDBLens: An Evaluatology-Based Framework for Vector Database Diagnosis
papers.summary: Framework attributing vector-DB performance to embedding, index or query execution.

papers.title: e-means: outperforming k-means (in one-tenth the epochs)
papers.curator_blurb: Meta introduces a mini-batch k-means with moving-average updates and scaling laws that set its hyperparameters, reaching lower loss than Lloyd's in far fewer epochs.
papers.summary: Meta's mini-batch k-means variant with moving-average updates and scaling-law hyperparameters.

papers.title: AntEmbed: Dual-Mode Multimodal Embedding Model for Efficient and Fine-Grained Retrieval
papers.curator_blurb: Ant Group introduces a multimodal embedding model with fast and reasoning-enhanced modes in one shared space, distilling the reasoning gains into the fast mode.
papers.summary: Ant Group multimodal embedding model with fast and reasoning-enhanced modes.

papers.title: Yuanbao-Reranker: Document-Grounded Synthesis and Preference Distillation for Text Reranking
papers.curator_blurb: Introduces 0.6B, 4B &8B text rerankers trained on document-grounded synthetic queries and teacher preferences.
papers.summary: 0.6B/4B/8B text rerankers trained on document-grounded synthetic data.

papers.title: MetaEncoder: Exploring the Limit of Bi-Encoders for Multimodal System One Decision Making with Natural Language Interface
papers.curator_blurb: Meta tests three scoring designs and builds a multimodal bi-encoder for decisions and retrieval.
papers.summary: Meta compares scoring designs for bi-encoders in decision-making with a natural-language interface.

papers.title: Beyond Ranking: Are Decision Models Calibrated Relevance Scorers?
papers.curator_blurb: Finds that relevance probabilities from decision models like Jev are not calibrated to human judgments. A two-parameter calibration fixes much of the error and supports per-query cut-offs.
papers.summary: Relevance probabilities from LLM decision models are not calibrated to human judgments.

papers.title: Process then Retrieve: Investigating the Origins of the Modality Gap in Vision-Language Models
papers.curator_blurb: Finds that vision tokens are much more semantically dense than text tokens, so early layers process text first.
papers.summary: Traces the VLM modality gap to vision tokens being much more semantically dense than text tokens.

papers.title: Exploiting Feature-invariant Scaling Laws for Efficient A/B Experimentation in Recommendation Systems
papers.curator_blurb: Meta uses scaling laws to predict full-scale A/B results for recommendation model changes from a few small-scale runs.
papers.summary: Meta predicts full-scale A/B results for rec models from feature-invariant scaling laws.

papers.title: Calibrating Document-Local Boundaries for Contextual Chunk Retrieval
papers.curator_blurb: Alibaba improves late chunking retrieval by separating the correct chunk from similar chunks in the same document, using an adaptive loss scale and chunk-aware attention during encoding.
papers.summary: Improves late-chunking retrieval by separating the right chunk from similar ones in the same document.

papers.title: Hybrid Product Search Without the Copy: Lexical, Semantic and Filtered Retrieval Served Directly from a Data Lake
papers.curator_blurb: Extends Apache Pinot with BM25 scoring and rank fusion, so hybrid search runs in SQL directly on Iceberg tables without a catalog copy.
papers.summary: BM25 + semantic + filtered retrieval served directly from a data lake (Apache Pinot).

papers.title: Proactive Dimension-Adaptive Denoising for Graph Collaborative Filtering via Representation Coherence
papers.curator_blurb: NetEase flags noisy interactions by their deviation from a user's preference centroid in embedding space.
papers.summary: Denoising graph CF by flagging interactions that deviate from a user's representation coherence.

papers.title: Sheaf-Inspired Structured Scoring Extensions of LightGCN for Collaborative Filtering
papers.summary: Sheaf-inspired scoring extensions of LightGCN.

papers.title: KuaiRecV2: Benchmarking Large-Scale Continual Learning for Diversified and Multi-task Recommendation
papers.comments: This paper has been accepted to NeurIPS 2026
papers.curator_blurb: Kuaishou releases a video benchmark for testing recommenders on continual learning, diversity, and multiple tasks.
papers.summary: Kuaishou benchmark for large-scale continual multi-task recommendation.

papers.title: TRIAD: Multimodal Retrieval across Abstraction, Constraints, and State
papers.curator_blurb: Introduces a multimodal retrieval benchmark on concept hierarchies, joint constraints, and multi-turn revisions. No system leads across all subsets.
papers.summary: Multimodal retrieval benchmark over concept hierarchies, joint constraints and state.

papers.title: DocFS: File Systems as Agentic Reasoning Environments for Complex Multimodal Document Question Answering
papers.curator_blurb: Turns documents into file systems with folders mirroring sections, so VLM agents find evidence using standard navigation, search, and read tools.
papers.summary: Documents turned into file systems as an agentic environment for multimodal document QA.

papers.title: CURATOR: Scalable Fine-grained Evidence Selection for Retrieval-Augmented Generation using Decision Models
papers.curator_blurb: Amazon presents a fine-tuned decision model that selects supporting spans from retrieved passages for RAG and stays reliable as candidates grow.
papers.summary: Amazon fine-tunes a decision model to select fine-grained evidence for RAG.

papers.title: From Search to Decision: How Post-Training Shapes Information-Seeking Capabilities in Large Language Models
papers.curator_blurb: Surveys how post-training teaches LLMs to decide when to search, write queries, and weigh evidence across six information-seeking skills.
papers.summary: Survey of how post-training teaches LLMs when and how to search.

papers.title: RMIT-ADM+S at TREC RAG 2026: Research Agents, Retriever Ablations, and Open-Weight Replication
papers.summary: RMIT at TREC RAG 2026: research agents, retriever ablations, open-weight replication.

papers.title: Lost in Delegation: Studying the Effectiveness of Task Orchestration in Generative Search
papers.summary: Studies task orchestration/delegation in generative search systems.

papers.title: Active Learning of Approximate LLM Ranking for Energy-Efficient Retrieval of Long Queries
papers.summary: Active learning of an approximate LLM ranker for energy-efficient retrieval of long queries.

papers.title: SurvEval: Listwise Re-Ranking Evaluator via Survival-Based Exposure and Multi-Objective Value Modeling
papers.summary: Listwise re-ranking evaluator built on survival-based exposure modelling.

papers.title: ReAlign: Reward-Guided Preference Alignment for Generative Re-Ranking
papers.summary: Reward-guided preference alignment for generative re-ranking.

papers.title: SimRec: Learning to Search, Ask, and Recommend from Simulated Interaction
papers.summary: Learning to search, ask and recommend from simulated interaction.

papers.title: When Does a Recommendation Spark Curiosity? Theory, Measurement, and Field Evidence
papers.curator_blurb: Proposes a measure of the curiosity an item evokes and a recommender based on it.
papers.summary: Axiomatises the information-gap theory of curiosity into a computable measure for recommendation, validated in a survey and field data.

papers.title: Characterizing Predictive Multiplicity in Ranking and Its Fairness Implications
papers.summary: Formal definitions and guarantees for predictive multiplicity in score-based ranking.

papers.title: Rethinking "RL Generalizes, SFT Memorizes": The Role of SFT Data
papers.summary: With the right data mix and matched rollout budget, SFT generalises as well as or better than RL.

papers.title: Rectified Looped Transformer
papers.summary: Interpolation between loops keeps hidden-state norms bounded in looped transformers; lower perplexity.

papers.title: Classical Energies Learn to Reason 1,000x Faster than Looped Models
papers.summary: A learned Hopfield–Tank energy solves Sudoku-Extreme/Maze ~1000× faster than looped models — a caution about these benchmarks.
